result.topic_en: Continuation of a case analysis (4th class, x and Y integers) for Gaussian-integer residues modulo a complex prime, defining the sign ε and the complexes Θ'' and Θ''' of numbers I+Vi by positivity conditions, with small numerical tables.
result.transcription:
$y$ | $X$ | $x^0$ | $Y^0$ | $t+ui$ | $\theta''$ | $\theta'''$ | $\varepsilon$
$0$ | $+1$ | $+4$ | $-2$ | $+2\quad 0$ | | $+2$ | $+1$
$+1$ | $+2$ | $-3$ | $-3$ | $-3+i$ | $+3-i$ | | $-1$

4te Classe $x$ und $Y$ Ganze
Nach ähnlichen Praemissen wie in 3 setze man
$-(t+ui) = Mp'-mP' = -\frac{Mp^0}{\alpha} + \frac{mP^0}{\alpha}$
$= -\frac{Miy^0}{\alpha} + \frac{mX^0}{\alpha}$

$\alpha t = -By^0 - aX^0$ $\quad y^0 = -bt + au$
$\alpha u = +Ay^0 - bX^0$ $\quad X^0 = -At - Bu$
Man hat dann
$\varepsilon = +1$ wenn $\alpha$ positiv, $y^0$ positiv, $X^0$ positiv, $t+u$ gerade &c.
Wir setzen
$t+ui = +\theta''$ wenn $y^0$ positiv $X^0$ negativ
$+\theta'''$ wenn $y^0$ positiv $X^0$ positiv
$-\theta''$ wenn $y^0$ negativ $X^0$ positiv
$-\theta'''$ wenn $y^0$ negativ $X^0$ negativ
für $\varepsilon$ gilt dann die Regel dass {+wie oben in 3+}
$\varepsilon = -1$ für jedes durch $1+i$ $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\text{theilbare } \theta'' \\ \text{untheilbare } \theta'''\end{array}\right.$ insofern $\alpha$ positiv
$\varepsilon = +1$ für jedes durch $1+i$ theilbare $\theta'''$ also {+unthei[?]+}

$x$ | $X$ | $y^0$ | $X^0$ | $t+ui$ | $\theta''$ | $\theta'''$ | $\varepsilon$
$+1$ | $+1$[?] | $-2$ | $-1$ | $-1\quad 0$ | | $+1$ | $-1$[?]
$+2$ | $+3$[?] | $+4$ | $-4$ | $+2-i$ | $+2-i$ | | $+1$

Der Complexus aller $\theta''$, [-aus-] 3 und 4 den wir durch $\Theta''$
bezeichnen [-hat-] besteht also aus allen Zahlen $I+Vi$, wofür
$\left.\begin{array}{l}-bI+aV \\ \text{und } +AI+BU\end{array}\right\}$ positiv und kleiner als $\frac{1}{2}\alpha$
der Complexus aller $\theta'''$ ... ($\Theta'''$) aus denen wo
$\left.\begin{array}{l}-bI+aV \\ -AI-BU\end{array}\right\}$ positiv und kleiner als $\frac{1}{2}\alpha$

methods.what: Expression of -(t+ui) in terms of p', P' and the reduced quantities y^0, X^0
Linear relations between t, u and y^0, X^0
methods.quote:
$\alpha t = -By^0 - aX^0$ $\quad y^0 = -bt + au$
$\alpha u = +Ay^0 - bX^0$ $\quad X^0 = -At - Bu$

methods.what: Classification of t+ui into ±θ'' or ±θ''' according to the signs of y^0 and X^0
Rule for the sign ε according to divisibility of θ'', θ''' by 1+i
Characterisation of the complexes Θ'' and Θ''' by inequalities on linear forms
Numerical tables of example values of x, X, y^0, X^0, t+ui, θ'', θ''', ε

items.english: ε = +1 if α positive, y^0 positive, X^0 positive, t+u even, etc.

items.quote:
für $\varepsilon$ gilt dann die Regel dass {+wie oben in 3+}
$\varepsilon = -1$ für jedes durch $1+i$ $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\text{theilbare } \theta'' \\ \text{untheilbare } \theta'''\end{array}\right.$ insofern $\alpha$ positiv
items.english: For ε the rule then holds (as above in 3) that ε = -1 for every θ'' divisible by 1+i and every θ''' not divisible by 1+i, insofar as α is positive.

items.english: The complex of all θ'' from 3 and 4, which we denote by Θ'', therefore consists of all numbers I+Vi for which -bI+aV and +AI+BU are positive and less than α/2; the complex Θ''' of those where -bI+aV and -AI-BU are positive and less than α/2.
